Beta4: highlights in WGL/EGL

Model-part colors no longer wash out in EGL/ANGLE. Palette, alpha and skin blending match WGL, including reflections. Item, held/world weapon, male/female/cyborg, MD2/MD5 and Bloom/HDR paths were checked. WGL cel outlines render after colored layers with depth testing; EGL uses pixel-width edges instead of an inflated shell. A new factory visibility preset is «Фиолетовые мужики, салатовые бабы».


Highlights and Bloom in beta 3

The Bloom menu combines overall strength with independent 0–100% category multipliers. 100% uses overall strength; 0% skips that category as a Bloom source. Comets retain their own controls. AVFX categories remain in this menu but are excluded from Visibility presets.

Overall strength and Bloom categories.

Fixed Bloom with zero fill opacity, uneven model contribution, RGB tint and male/female/cyborg skin replacement. Player parts can exclude outlines independently of fill. Highlights are reproduced in mirrors and puddles.

Visibility presets offer four shared custom slots and one-click random generation. They save highlights and ordinary Bloom, excluding skin overrides, player identity, downloads and AVFX Bloom categories. A factory preset disables all highlight masters. Applying a preset retains each variable's existing global/mod save scope.



Highlight fixes in beta 2

Using outline and fill together preserves their separate transparency instead of turning the item into an opaque color patch. Fixed temporal-stability and model-pass consistency errors. Reflections use the same highlight plan. No new setting is required to enable these fixes.


The general idea

Q2PRO-X highlights are a local visual layer. They change no server, no hitboxes, no damage, no movement and no network protocol. Their job is to make items, weapons and players easier to read, especially in demos, in practice, in single player and in visual presets.

To start quickly: enable the highlight layer, then configure items, weapons or players.

1.2. Items

Items have a style (off, shell, tint, shell and tint), opacity, shell opacity, shell thickness, brightness and scale. Item classes are enabled separately: health, armor, ammo, powerups and keys. Colours are configured per class.

The player style also has off, shell, tint and shell-and-tint variants, opacity, shell opacity and thickness, scale and brightness.

Player scale applies only in single player or while watching .dm2 and .mvd2 recordings. On a live server the model keeps its standard size.

3. Model parts

The Model parts mode colours parts of the model on the fly:

VariablePart
cl_vis_player_parts_head_colorHead
cl_vis_player_parts_arms_colorArms
cl_vis_player_parts_torso_colorTorso
cl_vis_player_parts_legs_colorLegs
cl_vis_player_parts_weapon_colorThe carried weapon

Both model paths are supported — MD2 and MD5. For MD5 the skeleton, the animation and the skin path are preserved: Q2PRO-X never falls back to MD2 for the sake of a highlight.

3.2. Separate sets per model

The colour set can be shared, or separate for the male, female and cyborg models. Each of the three models has its own part-colour page.

3.3. Tuning the body zones

Three sliders solve the most common problem — one zone's colour spilling into its neighbour:

if the head colour spills onto the shoulders, raise the head start;
if the legs reach into the torso, lower the legs end;
if the boundaries are too blurred, reduce the boundary softness.
VariableAccepted valuesDescription
cl_vis_player_parts_head_startdefault 0.86 / range 0.60..0.98Normalized height where the head tint starts. Increase this when the head colour leaks onto shoulders; decrease it if the lower head/neck is not coloured enough. Default 0.86 is tighter than the first Phase-A prototype.
cl_vis_player_parts_softnessdefault 0.035 / range 0.005..0.20Soft transition width for head/torso/legs classifier. Smaller values produce cleaner borders; larger values blend colours more gradually. Default 0.035 reduces head colour bleed on shoulders.



4. Commands, presets and diagnostics

cl_vis_items_info prints the item classification and the current state of the visibility layer.
The visibility presets are collected on their own page and give you ready-made profiles.
For a clean competitive look, keep highlights and AVFX separate: choose the AVFX preset first, then apply a visibility preset or configure it by hand.

4.1. Where highlighting applies

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
cl_vis_singleplayer0=multiplayer only / 1=also singleplayerAlso apply the visibility layer in singleplayer. When off, the highlight system only activates in multiplayer maps (cl.maxclients > 1) since most classic SP players dislike shell overlays on AI.

By default the layer is aimed at online play and at watching recordings. A separate setting permits it in single player as well.


5. Practical recipes

TaskSetting
Demo analysisModel parts mode, brightness 1.5–2.5, shell-and-tint style, moderate opacity
Single playerItem scale 1.3–1.8, weapon scale 1.2–1.5, permit the layer in single player
A good-looking showcasePart tint with pure colours off, so the skin texture is preserved
Maximum readabilityPure colours on, tint replacement on, bright head, torso and leg colours


6. What highlighting does not do

It does not change hitboxes and does not affect hit registration.
It does not show players through walls and reveals no hidden entities.
It does not change server rules and needs no server support.
It does not replace models or skins: it only colours what is already drawn.
